what: A converged free-space reference for A's body (FL-9 as the frozen model builds it, phase 0's floored pose with the wall left out: the error budget's free-space arm), its 6 x 6 resistance and axial speed (operating_point.speeds, the error budget's reported quantity), by two routes, with the free sphere (0.3 of A's tube radius) as the control of each. A diagnostic, not a register entry: no frozen choice changed, the register not edited, no measured speed read. Written before any solve of this study.

read_before_writing.error_budget_free_space: A's body in free space, axial speed (mm/s), spacings 0.2/0.16/0.128/0.1024 x blobs 0.25/0.35/0.5/0.7/1.0 (the error budget's grid, its report's table); its order-1 two-finest limits by blob 3.04/3.08/3.07/3.05/3.01
read_before_writing.prefit: computed before this file from those 20 points, never used for a verdict: U = U* + r eps + s eps^2 + h q0 exp(-kappa blob) (the sphere's structure, mean spacing h): U* 3.059 +- 0.018, r 0.31 +- 0.41 /mm, s -0.57 +- 1.9, q0 -11.3 +- 0.5, kappa 3.49 +- 0.16, rms 0.0115 mm/s; its split at the frozen point: regularisation +0.020, quadrature -0.288 mm/s
read_before_writing.local_spacing: computed before this file (the node's samples at 0.2/0.16/0.1024 mm): the lateral patch is Gauss-Legendre along the axis, so in the middle third of the body the square root of a sample's weight is 1.47 x the mean spacing (median; 1.69 x at most) and the nearest neighbour 0.96 x: the axial spacing on the flanks is about 2.2 x the mean spacing, the round's about 1 x. The ends and caps are denser (5th percentile 0.37 x).
read_before_writing.dry_run: the CPU dry run of these scripts (sizes outside the study's grid), before this file was committed: the in-place path against the node's 4e-16 to 6e-16 relative; the sphere's nearest-neighbour route at a 200-point force set within 1e-4 of the exact regularised drag at every eps (1.02117 against 1.021165 at eps0); A's body's nearest-neighbour route at force sets 0.5 and 0.4 mm 2.676 and 2.852 mm/s at eps0 (finest quadrature there 0.15 mm): a force-set dependence of 6.5% at those coarse sets

definitions.frozen_point: 0.16 mm nominal (mean spacing 0.14572 mm), blob 0.5, eps0 = 0.072858 mm; the node's free-space axial speed there 2.7979 mm/s (error budget)
definitions.eps_set_m: the frozen spacing's five blobs' eps (0.036429, 0.051001, 0.072858, 0.102001, 0.145716 mm), then 0.2 and 0.29 mm
definitions.route_a: the node's discretisation (point forces at its samples) in free space at 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1024, 0.092, 0.082 and 0.072 mm nominal, as far as XLA's plan fits, each blob 0.25-1.0, and each eps of the set (the node's fixed-eps lines). One matrix assembled in place and factorised by Cholesky; the node's own path (bem_budget.Case) beside it at blob 0.5 wherever four matrices fit, as its control.
definitions.route_b: Gallagher & Smith's nearest-neighbour discretisation: a fixed force set (the node's samples at 0.16 mm; then 0.2, 0.128, 0.1024, 0.092), collocation at the force points, one traction per force point's cell; the quadrature the body's own sampler at 0.03, 0.021, 0.015, 0.0106 mm nominal with its axial count x2.5 (about isotropic on the flanks; 0.33 M to 2.65 M points), each point to its nearest force point; the wrench on the quadrature. At each eps of the set: the quadrature refined at the frozen force set, then the force set refined: 0.2, 0.128 and 0.1024 at the two finest quadratures, 0.092 at the finest alone.
definitions.sphere_controls: the same two routes on the free sphere: route (a) at 0.2 ... 0.032 mm nominal; route (b) at force sets 0.2/0.16/0.128/0.1024 and the same quadrature spacings; the exact regularised drag (bem_budget.sphere_regularised_drag) at every eps; Stokes 1.
definitions.uncertainty_route_a: at each blob, L1 = order-1 Richardson in the mean spacing from the two finest levels, L1' = the same from the second and third finest, Lp = the three-point limit with its fitted order p; sigma_blob = max(|L1 - L1'|, |Lp - L1| when p lies in [0.5, 3]). Route (a)'s limit: the mean of L1 over blobs 0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0; sigma_a = max(the largest sigma_blob, half the range of those L1).
definitions.uncertainty_route_b: at each force set and eps, the finest quadrature's value with sigma_q = its change from the second finest (for 0.092 mm, the 0.1024 set's). U_reg(eps) = order-1 Richardson in the force set's mean spacing from 0.1024 and 0.092 mm; sigma_f = max(|L1 - L1'| (L1' from 0.128 and 0.1024), the largest sigma_q of the two). Route (b)'s limit: weighted least squares U_reg(eps) = U0 + a eps + c eps^2 over the seven eps; sigma_b = max(the fit's standard error of U0, |U0 - U0 of a linear fit over the four smallest eps|, the largest sigma_f).
definitions.control_rule: a route passes its sphere control when its limit lies within max(2 sigma, 0.5%) of Stokes' 1 and (route b) its U_reg(eps) within max(2 sigma, 0.1%) of the exact regularised drag at every eps; a route that fails gives no value at A. The helix's reference is claimed only when both routes pass and |U_a - U_b| <= 2 sqrt(sigma_a^2 + sigma_b^2); it is then their inverse-variance mean, with the larger of the combined sigma and half their difference.
definitions.item_4: quadrature error at the frozen point = U_node(0.16, blob 0.5) - U_reg(eps0) (computed when route (b) passes its control); regularisation error = U_reg(eps0) - the reference (estimated: it carries the eps -> 0 extrapolation); each in mm/s and %, with its sign, and the same for R_xx and R_x,Ox.
definitions.control_on_the_body: the sphere's nearest-neighbour force-set error is tiny (dry run), so its control cannot test route (b)'s force-set extrapolation on the helix. The discriminating control is on A's body itself: at eps 0.2 and 0.29 mm the node's fixed-eps lines (route (a)'s levels, point forces at the samples, a different discretisation of the same regularised problem) converge within route (a)'s levels; route (b)'s U_reg there must agree with their converged value within 2 combined sigmas (the lines' sigma: their last change). If it does not, route (b)'s U_reg at A is not claimed.

amendment_before_any_solve: Committed after e7fa182 and before any solve of the study. XLA's memory plan, computed on the CPU in a dry run (0.4 mm), holds two matrices for the factor and for the triangular solve (the factor's buffer is taken, but a temporary of one matrix remains), so the ladders change: route (a) at 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1024, 0.092, 0.082 (two matrices about 74 GB) and 0.072 (only if the device's plan holds one matrix); route (b)'s force sets 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1024 and 0.092 (finest quadrature alone). Every level records XLA's plan and the device's peak; a level whose plan exceeds the device's budget is not run.
